key_insight: PIKS extends kernel regression to physics-informed learning with universal consistency for linear differential constraints, even when the true solution is outside the RKHS.
engineering_relevance: For solid mechanics and FEM surrogate modeling, PIKS offers a closed-form, theoretically grounded alternative to PINNs that can enforce governing equations while remaining analytically tractable.
method: Impose linear differential constraints directly in a kernel learning objective.
Use universal kernels such as Gaussian or Matérn to guarantee asymptotic consistency.
Derive finite-sample error bounds via operator-theoretic analysis and source conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing PIKS is competitive with PINNs and traditional finite element methods.
watch_item: Performance guarantees rely on linear differential constraints and suitable source conditions, so implementation quality and kernel choice may strongly affect practical accuracy.
